question: Can an evidence-backed change make the browser neural network more accurate than the gradient-boosted trees on concrete strength?
answer: One change survived every check: giving the network four textbook strength laws as extra inputs. It lowered the error on two separate sets of eight held-out splits, but the gain is within split-to-split noise against the trees. On the page's own split it is level with the plain network. The page offers it as a switch, off by default.

method.tournament: Seven agents, one per literature MCP server, each found one idea, implemented it as an opt-in option in src/lib/nn.js, tuned it by 3-fold cross-validation on the 786 training rows only, and scored it at most three times on the eight selection splits. A second agent then re-ran the claim from the file, read the code for leaks and checked that the default ({}) was unchanged.
method.selection_splits: node scripts/experiments/make_splits.mjs . selection.json        (seeds 1001-1008, 80/20 by mix over all 1,005 lab results)
method.confirmation_splits: node scripts/experiments/make_splits.mjs . confirmation.json 2000   (seeds 2001-2008; no agent saw these; used once, to check the winner)
method.interval: Paired 95% t interval on the per-split differences. 'corrected' widens it for overlapping test sets (Nadeau and Bengio 2003): variance x (1/8 + 0.25).

the_change.option: features: 'physics', physicsOn: 'base', physics: ['abrams', 'bolomey', 'feret', 'bolomeyAge'], decay: 0.003, loss: 'huber'  (exported as PANEL_DESIGN)

inputs_added.feret: (binder volume / (binder volume + water))^2, binder volume from densities 3.15, 2.9 and 2.3
inputs_added.bolomeyAge: (equivalent cement / water) x exp(0.25 (1 - sqrt(28 / age))), the CEB-FIP / fib hardening curve for normal cement

the_change.equivalent_cement: cement + 0.9 slag + 0.4 fly ash. The 0.9 and 0.4 are the agent's own defaults, not values read from the papers below.
sources_checked_in_openalex: Yeh, I-C. (2013). Modeling Efficiency Factor of Fly Ash in Concrete Using an Unification Approach. International Journal of Engineering and Technology 5, 546-549. doi:10.7763/ijet.2013.v5.615 (OpenAlex W2328234545)
Babu, K. G. and Kumar, V. (2000). Efficiency of GGBS in concrete. Cement and Concrete Research 30(7), 1031-1036. doi:10.1016/s0008-8846(00)00271-4 (W2022106669)
Babu, K. G. and Rao, G. S. N. (1996). Efficiency of fly ash in concrete with age. Cement and Concrete Research 26(3), 465-474. doi:10.1016/s0008-8846(96)85034-4 (W2130323234)
the_change.default_unchanged: With options {} the file gives the same training history and predictions as before (checked by the re-run agent; the page's plain run still shows 3.9 MPa and +-11.1 MPa).

page_split_six_seeds.note: The page's own 786/219 split, seeds 11-16. MAE in MPa; water and age = tested mixes (of 26) where the prediction falls with more water and rises with age; below zero = mixes where the network predicted a negative strength somewhere.

browser_check: Built site, Chromium, seed 11. Switch off: 3.9 MPa, +-11.1 MPa, water 23 of 26, age 26 of 26, below zero on 6, about 7.5 s. Switch on: 4.0 MPa, +-10.3 MPa, water 20 of 26, age 26 of 26, below zero on 3, about 8 s. No console errors; no sideways scroll at 390 px.

other_lanes.note: Claimed by the exploring agent on the selection splits but NOT re-run by a second agent: those checks stopped at a usage limit. Treat as unverified.
other_lanes.priorwork (bagging, tanh, log target): 4.232: worse than the current ensemble; a clear negative result

what_not_to_say: Do not say the network beats the trees: against the trees every interval includes zero. Do not say the network understands concrete: it was handed the laws as inputs and only learned how much weight to give them.
